notes: Four rounds. R1 on 1e9918a, R2 on 553abd3, R3 on 297302e, R4 scoped to the 32-line test-only delta 9d4df71 (precedent: #317 round 8). Three of R2's four majors were introduced by R1's fixes, and two of R3's four by R2's. ADR-0070 section 4 never fired because no round produced a BLOCKING finding; the gain-based signal proposed in issue #319 section 5 WOULD have fired at R3. Escalated to the operator at the 3-round backstop ceiling; a Fable advisory review then established that a fourth CODE round buys no evidence, because the committed records' verdicts RE-DERIVE from their own raw per-trial observations through the committed predicate lib with zero mismatches (verified twice, independently). Four majors are therefore carried as open into issue #323, none of which can put a false statement in a durable artifact. Both DoD records carry repoDirty:true, which is the root of R3-MA1 and is addressed in #323.

findings.summary: a run with fewer than 3 trials overwrote the committed N=3 DoD record with a self-certifying N=1 record, and the header advertised that very invocation. Fixed in 568fdb2: N>=3 is now required (ADR-0022 section 5).

no observation-failure concept. 4 of 9 trials were killed at the run budget and scored PASS, so a process dying on its own would have been scored as a verdict about the gate. Fixed in 568fdb2 with a trial-validity state that distinguishes our own budget from a crash.

records pinned the model and the subjects but not the artifact under test, and the two records were produced by different revisions of the scenario with nothing saying so. Fixed in 568fdb2 and both records regenerated from one revision. The residual (the hash omits the predicate lib) is carried as R3-MA1.

leakGuard only printed to scrollback, so a run that breached isolation produced a record indistinguishable from a clean one. Fixed in 568fdb2 to invalidate the trial. That fix was itself defective: see R2-MA1.

the scenario deviates from the brain ruling it executes (1652256406c1 says the agent runs in the container and keeps dual-harness requirements) and disclosed it nowhere. Precedent covers the methodology; the silence was the defect. Disclosed in the header in 568fdb2 and the ADR-0022 scope claim softened in 297302e per R3-mi5.

the leakGuard rewritten by R1-M4 to be able to fail provably could not. String.includes is a substring test, so a genuine new line that is a substring of a baseline line was swallowed; and a REMOVED line produced no diff at all, removal being the signature of the plugin SessionEnd hook committing the brain, which is this scenario's own headline contamination. Both holes were executed and observed before fixing. Now a symmetric set difference, unit-mutated.

the arms could invalidate themselves BY SUCCEEDING: the sandbox probe ran after the agent, and the gate's identity check reads package.json, which the contrast and admit agents rewrite as a matter of course. Non-verdict invalidation was also unconditional across roughly 36 live gh calls per run, and the completeness flag ignored invalidTrials, so a no-verdict run would have overwritten the DEMONSTRATED record. Probe moved before the agent and scoped to gated arms; invalidation narrowed to load-bearing calls; a no-verdict run now routes to the partial record. The unguarded RED branch is carried as R3-MA2.

six predicates added by round 1, none ever observed firing: all sat at their inert value in every committed record (ADR-0070 section 2). The pure decision logic was extracted to scenarios/lib/p2-verdict.mjs with test/p2-verdict.test.ts, and all seven mutations were observed red rather than asserted. Four branches were still left unpinned: see R3-MA3.

a claude process that stalls at startup and is killed at our budget having done nothing was scored as a FAILED arm, which is a statement about the gate drawn from a trial in which no agent acted. Now invalid.

19 independent mutations of the new predicate lib found four surviving: redLetThrough without the refusals check and without the admissions check (the describe block was titled for the admitting half and never tested it), hasAllArms without its length check, and isDemonstrated without its completeness clause, without which a one-arm smoke run prints DEMONSTRATED and exits 0. All four confirmed surviving, then observed dying, in 9d4df71. Round 4 reproduced all four counts independently and killed eight further neighbouring branches.

scenarioSha256 hashes only the scenario, but round 2 moved the verdict predicates into scenarios/lib/p2-verdict.mjs, which nothing hashes, reopening R1-M3. This is NOT a false claim: the field states the scenario's own hash truthfully, nothing in the repo consumes it, and the verdict was independently RE-DERIVED from both records' raw per-trial observations through the committed lib with zero mismatches, which is stronger evidence than a hash. The root cause is hand-rolled hashes where a clean repoSha would do, plus repoDirty true in both records. Carried to #323.

recordName guards the scored record against being overwritten by a no-verdict run but leaves the RED branch unguarded, so a transient failure during a red re-run overwrites the committed can-fail evidence. The record written would be TRUE; the harm is the loss of prior true evidence, never a false claim. Carried to #323.

the sandbox-gate probe is a single-shot unretried live gh call whose non-verdict invalidates the trial. This is the same failure mode round 2 narrowed the non-verdict rule to avoid, not applied to the probe round 2 itself added. It discards a run and produces no claim, so it must be fixed BEFORE the next re-run rather than after. Carried to #323.

the record's model field is the REQUESTED constant passed via --model, never the observed one: the run uses plain-text -p with no json output format, so nothing reads back which model served the request. ADR-0050's own text names a pinned model appearing in modelUsage as THE example of observed-not-asserted, so this is the canonical case, inside the scenario that exists to satisfy that ADR. Not false, but asserted. Missed by all three adversarial rounds and surfaced by a Fable advisory review. Carried to #323.

run twice with identical results was asserted in the PR body and a brain entry but evidenced by nothing committed, the first record having been overwritten by the second. The claim was corrected rather than left standing.

m1 a comment described a materially worse experiment than the code performs, claiming the contrast arm has no settings file when removing it would add two confounds; m2 the generated hook's stated contract on outages disagreed with the pass logic; m3 wroteFiles blanket-filtered the .claude tree, a treatment-arm false-pass surface; m4 the RED predicate was satisfied by any treatment failure; m7 agreement between the sandbox gate and the precondition was assumed rather than asserted; m10 the RED record reused the demonstrated field as an inverted value. All fixed across 568fdb2 and 297302e.

leakGuard now trips if the operator's own session touches the real repo during a 25-minute run (fails safe); the settings.local.json filter is unconditional; m9 the generated hook declares no timeout so Claude Code's shorter default may kill it before the gate's own 120s, leaving no log line (fails safe, treatment would FAIL not falsely pass); m5 RED is N=1, defensible because the mutation is deterministic and precedent exists in pi-heal.red-baseline.json; m6 the isolation probe is N=1 and model-dependent (fails safe); mi9 wroteFiles slices porcelain output so a rename line is mis-parsed, cosmetic because only zero-versus-nonzero is load-bearing. All non-blocking and fail-safe.
